questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: France, and Paris in particular, has a strong history in mathematics, and Sorbonne Université offers some fairly specialized courses, more so than Copenhagen, in the fields I am most interested in. I certainly also liked the idea of living in Paris, having visited a few times before, and thought it would be great to improve my French.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Generally speaking, information from Sorbonne was not easy to find, lots of rules are not described anywhere in writing and will not be supplied to you unless you ask, so it is necessary to talk to secretaries, professors, etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a brief introductory session for all exchange students at the faculty, and the mathematics institute hosted an aperitif where there was also some time to clear up practical matters.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was offered housing from Sorbonne only after I had made arrangements myself, so I didn't take the offer. That said, I know that the university has an agreement with (among others) Fondation Deutsch de la Meurthe in Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris, which is a very nice place to live. I did live in the Cité, in the Danish house, Fondation Danoise, which I strongly recommend applying to.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I strongly recommend applying the Cité Universitaire or other student housing to avoid a very and cramped living situation (unless you are dead set on having an authentic Paris experience). The social life is also great.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Registration was a bit more complicated than it should have been as there are certain documents that you I needed to have signed that I was not told about until a very late time. However, the fact that it is not necessary to register until a few weeks into the courses made everything flexible enough.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process depends strongly on the specific program, even for the math master's programs there are different systems. For the M1 courses, registration is done through an online portal (for the first time  ever this year, I was told!) and for the M2 in pure mathematics (Math fonda), it is done through a google form. In both cases, exchange students are asked for an extra document which is to be signed by the person responsible for exchange students at the institute and handed in physically to the secretary.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You will not be offered any help unless you ask for it. The professor responsible for exchange students was very helpful with everything, the secretaries not so much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to register for all the courses I was planning on.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep asking if you are not given the information you need.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses in the M1 (first year of the master's) was generally quite low, comparable with some exceptions to the more advanced bachelor's courses in Copenhagen. There is a big jump to the M2 courses which are of similar difficulty to the harder Master's courses in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In math, teaching was done in more or less the same way I was used to with the exception that students were usually not expected to work on problems ahead of exercise classes. Instead, we would work on them in class. Also, lectures are 2 hours without any breaks which takes some getting used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Géometrie Differentielle (M1), Surfaces de Riemann (M2), Schémas I (M2).

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Topologie Algébrique (M1), Groupes et Algèbres de Lie (M1), Schémas II (M2), Champs Algébriques (M2).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: My favorite course was probably M2 Riemann Surfaces. The courses depend strongly on who is teaching them, I really enjoyed those taught by Benoît Stroh and François Loeser.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than I expected (probably in part due to inflation). Otherwise, expect similar prices to Copenhagen except that eating out is cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not look into it much

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in any in connection with the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Paris is a huge city, surely you will be able to find something that fits your interests.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not a problem

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: French students are not always very good at English, so it helps to be conversational in French.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I have no comments on this

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Keep asking if you are not getting the information you need
Make sure that your French level is good enough. In math, people students are generally allowed to do exams in English but this is absolutely not the case for every other program.
Attend your classes. While it's generally not compulsory at Sorbonne (unlike many other French universities), there is typically not as much information on lecture plans, syllabus, practicalities, etc. available online as you'll be used to from Copenhagen.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for housing at Fondation Danoise. It's a nice place to live, the social life is great, and there are plenty of opportunities do to sports or other activities in Cité Universitaire.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It's hard to pinpoint anything in particular, I learned a lot of math, made a lot of friends and generally had a good time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Exams for the M2 courses in pure math can be very hard, so don't expect to just breeze through even if you are used to that back home. I ended up having failing one and having to go to a re-exam despite working harder on the course than for many 12s I've got in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
